territorial_scope.description: Applies to consumer credit agreements under an EU directive, implemented through national transposition by each Member State.

evidence.quote: This Directive is addressed to the Member States.

summary.short: Harmonises EU rules on consumer credit agreements, covering credit information, advertising, creditworthiness assessment, database access, withdrawal, early repayment and caps, and supervision. Repeals Directive 2008/48/EC; Member States apply the measures from 20 November 2026.
summary.long: Directive (EU) 2023/2225 sets a harmonised framework for consumer credit agreements and repeals Directive 2008/48/EC. Addressed to Member States, it requires transposition by 20 November 2025 and applies from 20 November 2026. It covers most consumer credit, excluding among others mortgage-secured credit, credit above EUR 100 000 (renovation credit excepted) and certain employer or interest-free arrangements. Creditors and credit intermediaries must meet advertising standards, provide standard pre-contractual information, give adequate explanations, and assess creditworthiness before granting credit. Tying practices and unsolicited credit are prohibited. Where creditworthiness uses automated processing, consumers may obtain human intervention and an explanation. The directive also sets rules on credit databases, overdrafts and overrunning, withdrawal within 14 days, and early repayment compensation capped at 1% or 0.5% of the amount repaid. It requires forbearance measures and debt advisory referrals, staff competence, and admission or registration of non-credit creditors. Member States must introduce measures against excessive borrowing rates, such as caps, and designate competent authorities. Penalties must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive, and may include fines.

notes: This part covers the recitals and the operative Articles 1 to 50 as supplied, plus the footnotes. Annexes I to IV are referred to but are not included in this extract and are not annotated here. No registry IDs were supplied, so target_instrument_id is left empty. Recital 97 describes Directive 2008/48/EC as repealed and replaced; Article 47 repeals it from 20 November 2026 but keeps it applying to existing agreements until termination. Article 2(2)(l) also exempts credit agreements existing on 20 November 2026, with listed articles applying to open-end agreements. Relations and entities are the only sections annotated in this part; no events, thresholds, obligations, enforcement or definitions were coded. Part 2 covers Annexes I to IV only (standard information forms, APR equation and assumptions, correlation table) and contains no operative articles. Relations are limited to the repeal of Directive 2008/48/EC stated in the Annex I footnote; references to this Directive itself are not coded. Annex I (item 1) and Annex II (item 1) include a where-applicable line stating that the price was personalised on the basis of automated decision-making. Annex II omits the 14-calendar-day right-of-withdrawal sentence that appears in Annex I. Annex III II(h) assumes a ceiling of EUR 1 500 where the credit ceiling has not been agreed, as a calculation assumption. Creditor, credit intermediary and supervisory authority appear only as generic placeholders in square brackets, not as named bodies.

obligations.summary: Clear and comprehensible general information about credit agreements must be made available at all times on paper or another durable medium, and must include the listed elements (issuer identity, purposes, duration, rate types, representative example, further costs, repayment options, early repayment, withdrawal, ancillary services, general warning).

evidence.quote: clear and comprehensible general information about credit agreements is made available to consumers by creditors or, where applicable, by credit intermediaries, at all times

obligations.summary: Pre-contractual information must be provided in good time on the Standard European Consumer Credit Information form, with the prescribed elements on one page (two at most) and additional elements in a separate section; Annex I form and related content and consistency requirements apply.

evidence.quote: provide the consumer with the clear and comprehensible pre-contractual information needed to compare different offers

obligations.summary: Where pre-contractual information is given less than one day before the consumer is bound, a reminder of the right to withdraw must be sent between one and seven days after conclusion or submission of the binding offer.
obligations.conditional_on: where pre-contractual information is provided less than one day before the consumer is bound

evidence.quote: send a reminder to the consumer of the possibility to withdraw from the credit agreement

obligations.summary: On request, and where the creditor is willing to conclude the agreement, a copy of the draft credit agreement must be provided free of charge on paper or another durable medium.
obligations.conditional_on: upon consumer request

evidence.quote: provide the consumer free of charge with a copy of the draft credit agreement

obligations.summary: Where payments build capital rather than amortise credit, pre-contractual information must state that such agreements do not guarantee repayment of the total amount drawn, unless guaranteed expressly.
obligations.conditional_on: credit agreements where payments constitute capital rather than immediate amortisation

evidence.quote: include a clear and concise statement that such credit agreements do not provide for a guarantee of repayment

obligations.summary: For credit agreements under Art. 2(6) or (7), pre-contractual information must be given on the European Consumer Credit Information form (Annex II) with prescribed elements.
obligations.conditional_on: credit agreements referred to in Art. 2(6) or (7)

evidence.quote: shall, by way of derogation from Article 10(2), be provided on paper or on another durable medium chosen by the consumer

obligations.summary: Creditors and, where applicable, credit intermediaries must provide adequate explanations, free of charge and before conclusion, enabling the consumer to assess suitability, and must adapt them to the circumstances (Member States may adapt in justified cases).

evidence.quote: are required to provide adequate explanations to the consumer on the proposed credit agreements

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must inform consumers in a clear and comprehensible manner when presenting a personalised offer based on automated processing of personal data.
obligations.conditional_on: personalised offers based on automated processing of personal data

evidence.quote: inform consumers in a clear and comprehensible manner when they are presented with a personalised offer that is based on automated processing of personal data

obligations.summary: Member States must prohibit tying practices (credit offered only in a package where credit is not available separately) while allowing bundling practices.

evidence.quote: Member States shall allow bundling practices but shall prohibit tying practices.

obligations.summary: Where credit requires insurance, the creditor must accept an equivalent policy from a supplier chosen by the consumer; consumers must be given at least three days to compare insurance offers and are informed of this.
obligations.conditional_on: where the creditor requires a relevant insurance policy related to the credit

evidence.quote: the creditor is required to accept the insurance policy from a supplier different to his or her preferred supplier

obligations.summary: Personal data on consumers' oncological diagnoses must not be used for insurance policies related to credit after a period set by Member States, not exceeding 15 years after end of treatment.
obligations.conditional_on: after a period of time determined by Member States, not exceeding 15 years

evidence.quote: personal data concerning consumers’ diagnoses of oncological diseases are not used for the purpose of an insurance policy related to a credit agreement

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must not infer consumer agreement to credit or ancillary services from default options such as pre-ticked boxes.

evidence.quote: do not infer the agreement of the consumer for the conclusion of any credit agreement or for the purchase of ancillary services presented through default options

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must explicitly inform consumers whether advisory services are or can be provided, and before providing them give the listed information (basis of recommendation, fee) on paper or durable medium.
obligations.conditional_on: where advisory services are provided

evidence.quote: explicitly inform the consumer, in the context of a given transaction, whether advisory services are being or can be provided to the consumer

obligations.summary: Where advisory services are provided, creditors and credit intermediaries must obtain and update the consumer's financial information, assess needs, consider a sufficiently large number of agreements, act in the consumer's best interests, and give a record of the recommendation.
obligations.conditional_on: where advisory services are provided to consumers

evidence.quote: obtain the necessary information regarding the consumer’s financial situation, preferences and objectives related to the credit agreement

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must warn a consumer when a credit agreement may induce a specific risk given the consumer's financial situation.
obligations.conditional_on: where a credit agreement may induce a specific risk for the consumer

evidence.quote: warn a consumer when a credit agreement may induce a specific risk for the consumer considering the consumer’s financial situation

obligations.summary: Member States must prohibit any granting of credit to consumers without their prior request and explicit agreement.

evidence.quote: Member States shall prohibit any granting of credit to consumers without their prior request and explicit agreement.

obligations.summary: Before concluding a credit agreement the creditor must carry out a thorough creditworthiness assessment in the consumer's interest, based on relevant and accurate information (including joint repayment capacity for joint applications) and verified where necessary.
obligations.conditional_on: before concluding a credit agreement

evidence.quote: the creditor carry out a thorough assessment of the consumer’s creditworthiness

obligations.summary: Credit intermediaries must accurately submit the necessary consumer information to the relevant creditor so that the creditworthiness assessment can be carried out.

evidence.quote: credit intermediaries accurately submit the necessary information obtained from the consumer to the relevant creditor

obligations.summary: Creditors must establish, document and maintain procedures for the creditworthiness assessment and document and maintain the information used in it.

evidence.quote: Member States shall require the creditor to establish procedures for the assessment referred to in paragraph 1 and to document and maintain such procedures.

obligations.summary: Creditors may make credit available only where the creditworthiness assessment indicates the obligations are likely to be met.

evidence.quote: the creditor only makes the credit available to the consumer where the result of the creditworthiness assessment indicates

obligations.summary: Creditors must not cancel or modify a concluded credit agreement to the consumer's detriment because the creditworthiness assessment was incorrectly conducted, unless the consumer knowingly withheld or falsified information.

evidence.quote: the creditor shall not subsequently cancel or modify the credit agreement to the detriment of the consumer on the grounds that the assessment of creditworthiness was incorrectly conducted

obligations.summary: Where automated processing is used in the creditworthiness assessment, the creditor must allow human intervention, an explanation, the consumer's point of view, and review of the assessment and decision; consumers must be informed of this right.
obligations.conditional_on: where the creditworthiness assessment involves automated processing of personal data

evidence.quote: the consumer has the right to request and obtain from the creditor human intervention

obligations.summary: Where a credit application is rejected, the creditor must inform the consumer without delay and refer them to debt advisory services; where automated processing was used, the creditor must also inform the consumer of that and of the right to human assessment.
obligations.conditional_on: where the credit application is rejected

evidence.quote: the creditor is required to inform the consumer without delay of the rejection

obligations.summary: Before any significant increase in the total amount of credit after conclusion, the creditor must reassess creditworthiness on updated information.
obligations.conditional_on: where the parties agree to change the total amount of credit after conclusion and before any significant increase

evidence.quote: the creditor is required to reassess the consumer’s creditworthiness on the basis of updated information

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure that creditors from other Member States have non-discriminatory access to domestic creditworthiness databases in cross-border credit cases, for both public and private databases.
obligations.conditional_on: cross-border credit

evidence.quote: Each Member State shall, in the case of cross-border credit, ensure access for creditors from other Member States to databases used in that Member State for assessing the creditworthiness of consumers.

obligations.summary: Databases holding consumer credit information must hold at least information on arrears, type of credit and identity of the creditor; database providers must keep their information up to date and accurate.

evidence.quote: shall hold at least information on consumers’ arrears in repayment of credit, the type of credit and the identity of the creditor

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must not process special categories of personal data or personal data from social networks contained in creditworthiness databases.

evidence.quote: Creditors and credit intermediaries shall not process special categories of data as referred to in Article 9(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

obligations.summary: Where a credit application is rejected on the basis of a database consultation, the creditor must inform the consumer without undue delay and free of charge of the result, the database consulted and the categories of data used.
obligations.conditional_on: where the credit application is rejected on the basis of a database consultation

evidence.quote: the creditor informs the consumer without undue delay and free of charge of the result of such consultation

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure consumers are informed within 30 days of registration of any credit repayment arrears in a database, and of their rights under the GDPR.
obligations.conditional_on: registration of arrears in a credit database

evidence.quote: within 30 days of the registration of any arrears in repayment of credit in a database

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure complaint procedures exist to allow consumers to challenge the content of credit databases.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that complaint procedures are in place in order to facilitate consumers’ challenges to the content of databases

obligations.summary: Credit agreements and any modifications must be drawn up on paper or another durable medium, and all contracting parties must receive a copy.

evidence.quote: credit agreements and any modifications of such agreements are drawn up on paper or another durable medium and that all the contracting parties are provided with a copy

obligations.summary: Credit agreements must specify in a clear and concise manner the listed elements (e.g., type of credit, parties, amount, duration, borrowing rate, APR, payments, charges, withdrawal, early repayment, complaint mechanism, supervisory authority and debt advice contacts).

evidence.quote: the credit agreement specify in a clear and concise manner all of the following elements

obligations.summary: Where capital is amortised, the creditor must provide a free statement of account in the form of an amortisation table at any time; a statement that building capital does not guarantee repayment must be included where relevant.
obligations.conditional_on: where capital amortisation of a credit agreement with a fixed duration is involved

evidence.quote: the creditor shall make available to the consumer, free of charge and at any time throughout the duration of the credit agreement, a statement of account in the form of an amortisation table

obligations.summary: Before modifying the terms and conditions of a credit agreement, the creditor must communicate a description of the changes, timescale, complaint means and periods, and the competent authority for complaints.

evidence.quote: the creditor communicates on paper or another durable medium specified in the credit agreement the following information to the consumer

obligations.summary: Where creditors may change borrowing rates of existing agreements, they must inform the consumer of any change in good time before it takes effect, including the resulting payment amounts.
obligations.conditional_on: where creditors are allowed to change borrowing rates of existing credit agreements

evidence.quote: the creditor inform the consumer of any change in the borrowing rate on paper or another durable medium specified in the credit agreement, in good time before the change enters into force

obligations.summary: For overdraft facilities, the creditor must send at least monthly statements of account with listed elements, inform the consumer in good time of rate or charge increases, and notify reductions or cancellations at least 30 days in advance.
obligations.conditional_on: where credit is granted as an overdraft facility

evidence.quote: keeps the consumer regularly, at least once per month, informed by means of statements of account

obligations.conditional_on: where the overdraft facility is reduced or cancelled

evidence.quote: the creditor offer the consumer, before the enforcement proceedings have been initiated, at no additional cost, the possibility to repay the amount actually drawn down

obligations.summary: For overrunning, the creditor must include information on the overrun possibility and rates in the current account agreement, inform the consumer without delay of significant overruns exceeding one month, and notify non-allowance or reduction at least 30 days prior.
obligations.conditional_on: where there is a possibility that the consumer is allowed an overrun

evidence.quote: the creditor includes information on that possibility in that agreement

obligations.summary: In cases of regular overrunning, the creditor must offer advisory services where available and redirect the consumer at no cost to debt advisory services.
obligations.conditional_on: in the case of regular overrunning

evidence.quote: the creditor shall offer the consumer advisory services, where available, and redirect the consumer at no cost towards debt advisory services

obligations.summary: Where overrunning is reduced or cancelled, the creditor must offer, before enforcement, at no additional cost, repayment of the amount drawn in 12 equal monthly instalments unless repaid earlier.
obligations.conditional_on: where the overrunning is reduced or cancelled

evidence.quote: Where the overrunning is reduced or cancelled, Member States shall require that the creditor offer the consumer

obligations.summary: Consumers may withdraw from a credit agreement without giving reasons within 14 calendar days, with the period extended or limited as set out in the Article (including a 12-month-and-14-day long-stop where terms were not received).

evidence.quote: the consumer may withdraw from the credit agreement without giving any reason within a period of 14 calendar days

obligations.summary: A consumer exercising withdrawal must notify the creditor in the manner specified, and pay the capital and accrued interest without undue delay and no later than 30 calendar days after notification.
obligations.conditional_on: if the consumer exercises the right of withdrawal

evidence.quote: no later than 30 calendar days after the dispatch of the notification referred to in point (a)

obligations.conditional_on: where the consumer has exercised the right of withdrawal, based on Union law, concerning a contract for the supply of goods or services

evidence.quote: is no longer bound by a linked credit agreement

obligations.summary: For open-end credit, the consumer may terminate free of charge at any time (subject to notice not exceeding one month); the creditor may, where agreed, terminate with at least two months' notice.
obligations.conditional_on: open-end credit agreements; creditor termination only where agreed in the credit agreement

evidence.quote: the consumer may effect standard termination of an open-end credit agreement free of charge at any time

obligations.summary: Where the creditor terminates the consumer's right to draw down for objectively justified reasons, it must inform the consumer of the termination and reasons, where possible before and at the latest immediately after.
obligations.conditional_on: where agreed in the credit agreement and for objectively justified reasons

evidence.quote: The creditor shall inform the consumer of the termination and the reasons for it on paper or another durable medium specified in the credit agreement

obligations.summary: The consumer is entitled at any time to early repayment, with a reduction in the total cost of credit for the remaining duration that takes into account all costs imposed by the creditor.

evidence.quote: the consumer is at any time entitled to early repayment

obligations.summary: The annual percentage rate of charge must be calculated by the mathematical formula in Annex III Part I, as the present value of all commitments agreed.

evidence.quote: shall be calculated in accordance with the mathematical formula set out in Part I of Annex III

obligations.summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts to amend Article 30 and Annex III Part II by adding or modifying assumptions for calculating the APR.

evidence.quote: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 45

obligations.summary: Member States must introduce measures to effectively prevent abuse and ensure consumers cannot be charged excessively high borrowing rates, APRs or total costs of credit, such as caps; the Commission must make these measures public by 20 November 2027, and Member States must report to the Commission by 20 November 2026.

evidence.quote: Member States shall introduce measures to effectively prevent abuse

evidence.quote: By 20 November 2029 the European Banking Authority shall publish a report on the implementation of the measures referred to in paragraph 1

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must act honestly, fairly, transparently and professionally in manufacturing, advertising, granting, advising, ancillary services and executing credit; staff remuneration must not impede this and must avoid conflicts of interest and sales-target incentives.

evidence.quote: act honestly, fairly, transparently and professionally

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must require staff to possess and keep up to date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence in relation to credit products, intermediation, advisory services and consumer rights.

evidence.quote: creditors and credit intermediaries require their staff to possess and keep up-to-date an appropriate level of knowledge and competence

obligations.summary: Member States must establish minimum knowledge and competence requirements for staff of creditors and intermediaries and ensure competent authorities supervise compliance and can require evidence.

evidence.quote: Member States shall establish minimum knowledge and competence requirements for the staff of creditors and of credit intermediaries.

obligations.summary: Member States must promote consumer financial education on responsible borrowing and debt management; the Commission must assess and publish a report on financial education and best practices.

evidence.quote: Member States shall promote measures that support the education of consumers in relation to responsible borrowing and debt management

obligations.summary: Creditors must exercise, where appropriate, reasonable forbearance before enforcement proceedings, considering the consumer's individual circumstances, and need not offer forbearance repeatedly unless justified.
obligations.conditional_on: where appropriate, before enforcement proceedings are initiated

evidence.quote: Member States shall require creditors to exercise, where appropriate, reasonable forbearance before enforcement proceedings are initiated

obligations.summary: Where Member States allow creditors to impose additional charges on default, they must cap those charges.

evidence.quote: those Member States shall place a cap on those charges

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that independent debt advisory services are made available to consumers

obligations.summary: Creditors must have processes and policies to detect early consumers experiencing financial difficulties and must refer them to easily accessible debt advisory services.

evidence.quote: creditors shall have processes and policies in place for the early detection of consumers experiencing financial difficulties

obligations.summary: Creditors and credit intermediaries must be subject to an adequate admission process, registration and supervision by an independent competent authority, subject to listed exemptions for credit institutions, payment and e-money institutions and ancillary micro and SME suppliers.

evidence.quote: creditors and credit intermediaries are subject to an adequate admission process, to registration and to supervision arrangements set up by an independent competent authority

obligations.summary: Credit intermediaries must indicate in consumer-facing advertising and documentation the extent of their powers and whether they work exclusively with one or more creditors; must disclose and agree fees with consumers before conclusion and communicate fees to the creditor for APR calculation.

evidence.quote: indicate, in advertising and documentation intended for consumers, the extent of their powers

obligations.summary: The original creditor must inform the consumer of an assignment of the credit agreement, except where it continues to service the credit with the assignee's agreement.
obligations.conditional_on: assignment of creditor's rights, unless original creditor continues servicing the credit

evidence.quote: Member States shall require that the original creditor inform the consumer of the assignment referred to in paragraph 1

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure consumers have access to adequate, prompt and effective out-of-court dispute resolution procedures and encourage cross-border cooperation between such entities.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that consumers have access to adequate, prompt and effective out-of-court dispute resolution procedures

obligations.summary: Member States must designate national competent authorities with investigation and enforcement powers and adequate resources, and notify the Commission of designations by 20 November 2025.

evidence.quote: Member States shall designate the national competent authorities empowered to ensure the application and enforcement of this Directive

obligations.summary: Competent authorities and persons working for them, and auditors and experts instructed by them, are bound by professional secrecy, subject to exceptions in law.

evidence.quote: are bound by the obligation of professional secrecy

obligations.summary: The Commission must publish a list of competent authorities in the Official Journal at least once a year and update it on its website.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall publish a list of the competent authorities in the Official Journal of the European Union at least once a year

obligations.summary: Where the Directive contains harmonised provisions, Member States may not maintain or introduce national provisions diverging from them, unless the Directive provides otherwise.
obligations.conditional_on: insofar as the Directive contains harmonised provisions

evidence.quote: Member States may not maintain or introduce in their national law provisions diverging from those laid down in this Directive

obligations.summary: Where a Member State uses the listed regulatory choices, it must notify the Commission without delay and of subsequent changes.
obligations.conditional_on: where a Member State uses the regulatory choices listed in Article 42(2)

evidence.quote: that Member State shall notify the Commission without delay thereof, as well as of any subsequent changes

obligations.summary: Consumers may not waive the rights conferred by the national measures transposing the Directive.

evidence.quote: consumers may not waive the rights conferred on them by the national measures transposing this Directive

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure that transposing provisions cannot be circumvented through the way agreements are formulated.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that the provisions adopted in order to transpose this Directive cannot be circumvented

obligations.summary: Member States must notify the Commission of their penalty rules and measures by 20 November 2026, and notify any subsequent amendment without delay.

evidence.quote: Member States shall, by 20 November 2026, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures

obligations.summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under Article 30(5) is conferred on the Commission for five years from 19 November 2023, tacitly extended unless opposed; the Commission must draw up a report not later than nine months before the end of that period.

evidence.quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 30(5) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 19 November 2023.

obligations.summary: The Commission must evaluate the Directive by 20 November 2029 and every four years thereafter (scope, thresholds, compensation percentages, green-transition credit, penalties), and assess consumer protection for crowdfunding by 20 November 2025.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall undertake, by 20 November 2029 and every four years thereafter, an evaluation of this Directive.

obligations.summary: Member States must adopt and publish the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the Directive, and immediately communicate their text to the Commission.

evidence.quote: Member States shall adopt and publish, by 20 November 2025, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.

obligations.summary: Member States must apply the transposing measures from 20 November 2026.

evidence.quote: They shall apply those measures from 20 November 2026.

obligations.summary: Member States must communicate to the Commission the text of the main national law measures they adopt in the field covered by the Directive.

evidence.quote: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.

evidence.quote: the creditor must fill in the box if the information is relevant to the type of credit

evidence.quote: The creditor must inform you immediately and without charge of the result of consulting a database

obligations.conditional_on: Upon consumer request; creditor willing to proceed to conclusion of the agreement

evidence.provision: Annex I, Part 3, 'Right to a draft credit agreement'
evidence.quote: You have the right, upon request, to obtain a copy of the draft credit agreement free of charge.

obligations.summary: Form note (1) to Annex II (debt conversion form): creditor must fill in boxes where information is relevant to the credit type, or delete information or rows where not relevant.

evidence.quote: the creditor must fill in the box if the information is relevant to the type of credit

obligations.conditional_on: Calculation of the annual percentage rate of charge

evidence.quote: The result of the calculation shall be expressed with an accuracy of at least one decimal place.

enforcement.triggered_by: Penalties imposed in accordance with Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2017/2394
